assertions.assert: On start, and only then, it sends `bot.ability.ready` to its parent (decision D242), with no data: it offers nothing, and a later entry into `idle` sends nothing more.

`bot.ability.vocal.speech.encoding.input` `{parts}` (1 to 64 parts `{expression?, words?}`) in `idle` is encoded by the speech service's `encode` with the `<param>`s `parts`, `model`, `voice`, `output` (the `<param>` `output_prefix`, the utterance's number counted from 1, and `.` and the media subtype) and `media_type` (`audio/pcm` by default); with provider `null` (the default) that is the OpenAI-compatible `POST {base}/audio/speech`. The service's answer is sent to the parent as `bot.ability.vocal.speech.encoding.output` `{audio, media_type, sample_rate_hz, channels, duration}` (the audio as the `output` reference; raw PCM is 24 kHz mono, its duration measured from its bytes; a format the service cannot measure has `null`s), and it returns to `idle`.

The `provider` `<param>` names another provider instead: `elevenlabs` is `POST {base}/text-to-speech/{voice}/stream?output_format=…`, `gemini` is `POST {base}/interactions` (its answer's base64 audio part), each answered as above.

When the service answers `bot.ability.failed` `{message}` (an error status, an empty answer, an `output` that cannot be written), it sends the parent `bot.ability.failed` with the service's message and returns to `idle`.

When the service cannot run (a missing `voice`, rejecting its start with `error.execution`), it sends the parent `bot.ability.failed` `{message: "The speech service could not run (<error event>)."}` and returns to `idle`.
An input that arrives while `applying` is dropped: only the input in hand is encoded and answered.
Each input is a new encoding: after an answer or a failure, the next input in `idle` is encoded again.

The service says the parts (decision D178): walking them in order, a part with a pause opens a new stretch, each stretch whose words are not blank is one backend request saying its words joined as written, one at a time in order, and no other cue (a sound, an emotion) is applied. With a pause the answers are joined as 16-bit PCM with each pause's silence at its place (0.4 s short, 1 s long), written raw for `audio/pcm` or in a WAV container for `audio/wav`; a pause with another `media_type` rejects the service's start, answered as in statement 5.

It is long-lived: `bot.ability.processing.cancel` `{}` while `applying` cancels the utterance in hand (the service call with it) and answers nothing; in `idle` it is dropped. The cancelled call's late events are not the next utterance's, which is encoded and answered as any.

The service streams its encoding (decision D203): each `bot.ability.vocal.speech.encoding.chunk` `{audio, sequence, media_type, sample_rate_hz, channels, duration}` it returns while `applying` is sent to the parent at once, as it arrives, before the output: its audio is chunk `sequence`'s own file (the `output` reference with `.<sequence>` before its extension), a streamed answer is cut into 4800 bytes (a tenth of a second of 24 kHz mono PCM) first and each chunk after it half again as long, in whole twentieths of a second, up to 24000 bytes (half a second; decision D280), Gemini's answer is one chunk per stretch, and a pause is a chunk of its silence.
